column1: # HAND-MAINTAINED. For every item our own logic treats as the key to a VANILLA PHYSICAL DOOR, this
# records WHAT THE GAME READS when the player tries that door -- an "obtained" event flag, or plain
# inventory possession -- and the evidence for the claim.
# WHY IT EXISTS. The client grants goods into the inventory. Some vanilla gates do not read the
# inventory: they read a dedicated "obtained" event flag that a raw grant never trips. When that
# happens the player holds the key, the door stays shut, and NOTHING tells anyone -- not the player,
# not us. That has now happened three times (Rold Medallion 400001, 2026-06-19, proven in game;
# the whetblade affinity flags, #240; and -- reported by a player on 0.2.18 and still open --
# Leyndell's Great Runes and the Academy Glintstone Key). Each was found by a person walking into a
# wall, because the client's table (crates/eldenring-archipelago/src/keyitems.rs) is a WHITELIST
# This file makes the silence loud. `tests/test_gf_key_item_gate_classification.py` DERIVES the
# population from the features themselves -- natural_progression.GATE_CLAUSES, legacy_key_gates
# -- and fails if any member is missing a row here. You cannot add a gate and forget this file.
#   obtained_flag      the gate reads an event flag. The client MUST set it on receipt. flags = the ids.
#   possession         the gate reads the inventory. A plain grant is enough. flags = "-".
#   not_a_vanilla_gate our logic uses the item as a region token; the game has no door for it. flags = "-".
#   UNVERIFIED         we have not established which. Counted by the ratchet below; not safe, just honest.
#   in_game    someone walked it, in our client. The only tier that closes the question.
#   datamine   read out of params/EMEVD/ESD or itemevents.txt. Strong; not proof of our grant path.
#   assumed    reasoning only. LEGAL ONLY ON `UNVERIFIED` -- a confident row must cite something.
# 🛑 UNVERIFIED IS DEBT, NOT A RESTING PLACE. The test pins the count and lets it only go DOWN.
# Do not reclassify a row to make the number smaller; move it by measuring it.

EMEVD probe 2026-08-01 + Alaric's ruling 2026-08-06 (#427) and 2026-08-16; GATE DERIVATION CORRECTED 2026-08-22 (clients#392). The wall counts the POSSESSION band 170-179, not the restored band 190-199 as this row claimed: the 王都の封印 (m60_45_52_00/.10 $Event(1045522500)) reads `EventFlag(182) && EventFlag(105)`; 182 is common $Event(730) slot 2 = `CountEventFlags(EventFlag, 170, 179) >= 2`. This rune differs from 191-196: those are Divine-Tower RESTORE flags (common 90005110, which CONSUMES the goods), and there is no Divine Tower for the Unborn rune. 197 is Rennala's ACQUISITION flag -- her drop awards goods 10180 (Remembrance) + 10181 (this rune, goods 10080). It advances the wall through one-shot relief $Event(6905) 救済対応_伍, which maps 197 -> 177 (and the other six runes' lot-obtained flags 510xxx -> 171-176) into the counted band -- so the kill alone advances the wall, via 177, not via 197 sitting in 190-199. 🛑 OPEN ITEM, ALARIC'S CALL, NOT SAFE TO GUESS AT: keyitems.rs writes 191-196 and has NO entry for this rune, and the obvious fix (writing 197) COLLIDES -- flag 197 backs our own co-check ap 7900004, so writing it may spend that check (quest flags double as lot awards). For the GATE the gap is moot while keyitems.rs writes 105+182 directly at >=2 AP-received runes; what a 197 write would add is the game's own acquisition state. The fallback previously noted here (write 190/198/199 as unaccounted band members) is DEAD under the corrected derivation -- nothing reads the restored counter's outputs 160-167, so those flags open nothing. Until ruled on, the flag recorded here is what the GAME reads, not what we write.
